added.description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.
CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.
If you are NOT a current employee or student, please click “Apply” and complete the application process for external applicants.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants.

POSITION SPECIFICS

The Pennsylvania State University’s College of Health and Human Development invites applications for an open-rank tenure-track position under its ongoing program area in environmental health sciences initiative. Applicants should have research interests that align with one or both of the following priority areas:

Built environment and health outcomes - the study of the influence of human-made surroundings on health and well-being of populations. Our principal interest is in population-level inquiry that involves (or spans) epidemiologic or computational (digital twins, agent-based modelling) approaches to assessing the influence of the chemical and material, biologic, physical, and geospatial exposures related to the built environment on health outcomes. Outcomes of interest should relate to other college research priorities including physical activity, mental health and well-being, substance misuse, cognitive decline, nutritional status, chronic disease etc. Scholars who bring an environmental health policy perspective to these issues are also welcome to apply. Successful candidate’s formal training background could be from a range of disciplines including, but not limited to environmental health science, epidemiology, environmental/health policy, human biology, urban planning, architectural engineering.
Extreme weather and health outcomes - the study of the influence of extreme weather (e.g., drought, extreme heat, flooding, hurricanes) and associated events on health and well-being of populations, such as but not limited to birth and developmental outcomes, nutritional outcomes, epigenetics, aging outcomes, physical activity, stress and inflammation, mental health, cardiometabolic health, etc. Our principal interest is in population-level inquiry that is consistent with the priorities in NIH’s Health and Extreme Weather Strategic Framework. However, researchers focused on mechanisms underlying the above associations (e.g., thermoregulation impacts on physiology) are also welcome to apply. Successful candidate’s formal training background could be from a range of disciplines including, but not limited to environmental health science, epidemiology, human biology, meteorology, or climate science.

Successful candidates will be expected to build research programs involving collaboration across multiple disciplines to both capitalize on the broad range of scientific expertise at Penn State University and to promote an understanding of environmental influences on health that considers interactions with social, behavioral, and physiological determinants. Tenure track faculty members at Penn State are also expected to teach, mentor trainees, and engage in service to the university and profession.

The primary academic appointment for this position will be in one of the College of Health and Human Development’s eight academic units, including but not limited to the departments of Biobehavioral Health, Kinesiology, Nutrition Sciences, Human Development and Family Science, and Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management. HHD is one of the larger academic units at the University, home to approximately 160 full-time faculty and 200 staff members who serve approximately 4,300 undergraduate and 300 graduate students in-residence at its University Park campus, as well as 600 online students at Penn State’s World Campus. In addition to its eight academic units, the college houses three research centers, and the college’s investigators lead projects generating ~$80 million in externally supported research expenditures.

As appropriate, offered positions may also be supported by one (or more) of the following university-level research institutes: Institute of Energy and the Environment (IEE), the Social Sciences Research Institute (SSRI), or the Cocoziello Institute of Real Estate Innovation as well as academic units in other colleges. Successful candidates co-funded by these institutes would attract extramural funding, publish in top journals, be collaborative and promote and enhance excellence and innovation in interdisciplinary research. For IEE, the focus would be on Institute’s Health and the Environment theme (one of IEE’s five key research themes). For SSRI, the candidate would emphasize research in social and behavioral sciences and be involved in broader University-wide activities, including those Penn State’s land grant mission. For Cocoziello, the research would center on how buildings and infrastructure are designed, constructed, and operated, how these structures create healthy, sustainable, and affordable housing solutions, and how they enhance living environments and accessibility for diverse communities.

Penn State is committed to and accountable for advancing equity, respect, and belonging. We embrace individual uniqueness, as well as a culture of belonging that supports equity initiatives, leverages the educational and institutional benefits of inclusion in society, and provides opportunities for engagement intended to help all members of the community thrive. We value belonging as a core strength and an essential element of the university’s teaching, research, and service mission.

Our campuses are located on the original homelands of the Erie, Haudenosaunee (Seneca, Cayuga, Onondaga, Oneida, Mohawk, and Tuscarora), Lenape (Delaware Nation, Delaware Tribe, Stockbridge-Munsee), Monongahela, Shawnee (Absentee, Eastern, and Oklahoma), Susquehannock, and Wahzhazhe (Osage) Nations. As a land grant institution, we acknowledge and honor the traditional caretakers of these lands and strive to understand and model their responsible stewardship. We also acknowledge the long history of these lands and our place in that history.

TO APPLY
- Applicants must demonstrate excellence in research, a strong publication record, and interest in collaboration across disciplines. Candidates must hold a PhD in one of the fields listed above. Established researchers should have demonstrated a track record of external grant funding and a commitment to mentoring students or early career researchers with early career researchers demonstrating the potential to achieve the above. An online application should be completed and upload, including: 1) a cover letter (3 pages max), which specifically addresses the job requirements and outlines qualifications, discusses which department(s) would be suitable as the tenure home, current and future research interests (including highlighting key publications and current/future funding plans), and how they would interact with one or more of the co-funding institutes, teaching philosophy, and a commitment to fostering diversity, equity, and inclusive excellence), 2) curriculum vitae, and 3) contact information for three (3) professional references who will be providing letters if applying at the assistant professor level or four (4) if applying at the associate or full professor level. We will request reference letters, with a short timeframe for response, only for applicants undergoing further consideration. Applications received by November 20 will be given full consideration, but applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled. Employment will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with university policies.

Inquiries
about the position may be directed to Dr. Asher Rosinger, Associate Professor of Biobehavioral Health and Anthropology, Environmental Health Sciences Program Area Leader, and Search Committee Chair, at axr579@psu.edu or 814-865-5220.

added.description:
Golden State Water Company is one of the largest investor-owned water utilities in the United States. We deliver quality, reliable water to more than 1 million people in over 80 communities throughout California. Golden State Water has been in business for more than 90 years because we put customers first.

POSITION DEFINITION AND ACCOUNTABILITY

Under minimal supervision, performs complex professional and administrative work in coordinating and supervising the water quality department. The incumbent is also responsible for directing the activities of supervisory and technical staff. Employee must also exercise tact and courtesy in contact with regulatory agency officials, public officials, public, and other stakeholders. The work of this class involves significant accountability and decision-making responsibilities. To ensure performance standards of this job, the individual must be able to execute each essential duty to meet the requirements listed below. These functions are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required for the Manager.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Directs water quality efforts to ensure that the company complies with all water quality and environmental regulations and programs within each system.
Establishes and implements water quality standards, procedures and controls to ensure effective water sample collection and testing, treatment and compliance.
Provides oversight of all compliance activities including the timely acquisition of water quality related permits and permit amendments
Develops, monitors, and manages key performance indicators relative to optimized water quality programs and compliance with standards and regulations
Attracts, hires, trains, and develops technical and supervisory staff in the Water Quality department
Represents Golden State Water in state and national industry associations or advisory groups, as needed
Monitor, evaluate, and provide feedback and comments on proposed regulations or policy related to water quality that may impact Golden State Water
Provide relevant and accurate water quality data and information in preparation of asset planning documents and capital budgets
Participate and provide support in preparation of testimonies and justifications for water quality related projects in General Rate Case filings
Responsible for overall management of specialized water quality projects and studies
Manages department personnel and monitors departmental budget.
Develop and maintains positive relationships with applicable regulatory agencies
Communicates, both orally and written, with applicable regulatory agencies, Company management and staff and others
Develops and maintains an effective employee relations plan; evaluates the performance of assigned personnel
Ensures Water Quality Department is in compliance with Company policies and procedures
Acts for the Vice President as directed
Works under minimal direction/supervision
Performs other duties as assigned

COMPETENCIES, WORKFORCE PLANNING, PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT

The Manager is competent in leading, motivating and developing staff in assigned areas of responsibilities with the ability to build shared commitment to improving business performance, and developing both individual and team capabilities. The incumbent is skilled in driving performance by linking business units' objectives to Company goals and values, including the ability to communicate a shared vision, energize and empower staff, and champion diversity.

Business Planning and Knowledge:
Competent of the utility industry priorities for ensuring that regulatory and company requirements and commitments are met with respect to the Water Quality Department. Extensive knowledge of the applicable regulations, requirements and trends impacting water quality and the water business, including assessment of current practices and the establishment of best practices.

Personal Credibility:
Demonstrated history of building and maintaining external and internal relationships. Skilled in supporting and assisting senior leadership in maintaining and enhancing such relationships state-wide with the ability to gain credibility and partnership with business leaders and peers in the industry. The Manager has strong history of consultative, interpersonal, communication and presentation skills to improve quality and outreach to regulators and other stakeholders.

Communication and Management:
Strong management skills (planning, organizing, analysis, problem solving, team working, employee development). Excellent leadership skills, with the ability to deal effectively with and maintain productive relationships with employees at all levels, senior management and various external stakeholders. Ability to lead, motivate and empower employees. Excellent written and verbal communications, as well as interpersonal skills (persuasion, listening, cooperation, diplomacy). Strong influencing skills.

Data and Trend Analysis:
Competent in the use of business metrics to measure program success. The Manager has the ability to use data to identify trends, patterns, issues and opportunities that impact the company’s customers.

Technology
: Skilled in a variety of technology and media platforms with proficiency in Microsoft Office products and other databases.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or Science related discipline
Graduate Degree in Engineering or Science related discipline preferred
Individual must have 10 years of progressively responsible experience performing highly complex work in the area of water quality, environmental engineering, regulations and operations.
Supervisory and leadership experience required
Water utility experience preferred.
Valid California drivers’ license.
May include but not limited to standing, walking, bending, pulling and/or pushing, grasping, lifting, reaching, stooping and crouching, color determination, typing, sitting, reading, speaking and listening

QUALITIES OF A SUCCESSFUL MANAGER IN THIS POSITION

Displays high standards of ethical conduct; exhibits honesty and integrity
Demonstrates strong level accountability and ownership
Works and communicates with internal and external stakeholders, clients, contractors, vendors and customers to meet their needs in a polite, courteous, and cooperative manner
Committed to quality service
Responds appropriately to supervision
Aligns behavior with the needs, priorities and goals of the organization
Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity
Fosters commitment and team spirit
Expresses information to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information
Emotional Maturity

Must be willing to travel up to 10% of the time!

Benefits

Our Company supports our employees with rich benefit programs and resources to help them thrive today and prepare for tomorrow. Benefit options include medical, dental, and vision plans with the Company currently paying 85% of the monthly premium for employees and their eligible dependents. We also offer paid vacation and sick time and twelve Company paid holidays per year. To help our employees plan for the future, we offer both a 401(k) retirement plan as well as a Defined Contribution Profit Sharing retirement plan. Additional benefits include life, AD&D, and LTD insurance as well as health savings account and flexible spending plans.

The compensation range provided is in compliance with state specific laws. Multiple factors are used to determine the actual starting rate of pay for all of our positions, including specific skills, years of experience, education, certification(s), and other job related factors.

added.description:
Job Title: Environmental Scientist III

Location: Billings, MT or Helena, MT

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL (HydroGeoLogic, Inc.) is seeking an Environmental Scientist III
based in our Billings, MT or Helena, MT offices. This position will support U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Montana DEQ, and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers environmental projects primarily in the Mountain West region. Projects commonly involve investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater and soil impacted by emerging contaminants (PFAS), chlorinated solvents, and petroleum compounds as well as abandoned mine lands.

Responsibilities/Duties

What You'll Be Doing

The person hired for this role will be responsible for:

Ensuring field operations are conducted in a safe manner in accordance with project specific Site Safety and Health Plans / Health and Safety Plans, design specifications, and standard operating procedures.
Managing / leading field teams for collection of water, soil, and soil vapor samples utilizing various sampling techniques.
Assisting with remedial system installation and operations & maintenance services.
Performing / conducting field subcontractor oversight inclusive of remediation, waste transportation and disposal, and heavy equipment operation.
Interfacing with program and project managers, senior technical staff, the government customer, and RA Contractors.
Contributing to the preparation of work plans and project deliverables (e.g., UFP-QAPPs, RI Reports, SSHP/HASPs, power point presentations, and technical memoranda).
Provide technical support during investigation, planning, design, implementation, and completion project phases.
Assisting with data entry, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical and visualization tools.
Managing or leading field teams collecting general field data, completing environmental sampling, and managing remedial systems.
Potential for up to 50% travel within the U.S. (primarily in western U.S.) will be associated with this position.
Utilize approved digital and AI-assisted tools, where appropriate, to support technical documentation, data analysis, project communications, and workflow efficiency.
Review of specifications, drawings, work plans, and ongoing construction activities to assure compliance during RA construction oversight.

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

The ideal candidate will need the following as a foundation for success in this role:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Geology, or Environmental Science-related field.
4+ years of experience.
Ability to work in a team environment with corporate, project, and technical management staff.
Excellent written and oral communication skills and organization.
Proficient in MS Word, MS Excel, and other MS Office applications.
Possess or have ability to obtain OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification upon employment.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.
Knowledge and experience of CERCLA, DoD, DOE, EPA, and/or RCRA projects.
Understanding of remediation and construction site health & safety (H&S) hazards.
Strong technical writing and documentation experience with prior experience contributing to the preparation of remedial design documents that are technically sound and accurately reflect the project approach and requirements.
Ability to conduct completion inspections, document project status and maintain records.
Working knowledge of federal and state occupational regulations.
Ability to prepare daily reports documenting activities and findings.
Excellent interpersonal communication skills (both written and oral) including the ability to comfortably engage with varying levels of leadership, RA Contractors, subcontractors, internal and external stakeholders, etc.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple priorities with attention to detail.

Desired Qualifications

WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required

Masters degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological/Geotechnical Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or a related field.
Experience working with EPA on mining related projects and/or Montana Department of Environmental Quality.
Experience as a Task Manager or Field Team Leader for environmental investigations and/or remediation projects.
PFAS sampling or remediation experience.
Remediation system design and/or installation experience.
Previous experience with characterization and remediation of abandoned mine land sites.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIRMENTS

A bility to lift/move/relocate items up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time
Prolonged standing up to 70% of the time
Walking long distances
Repetitive hand motions (typing, tool use, etc.)
Walking over uneven or mountainous terrain
Ability to see details at close range
Viewing computer screen for extended periods
Ability to interpret and analyze visual data (maps, graphs, warning indicators, etc.)
Driving a company or personal vehicle
Analyzing and synthesizing data
Complex problem solving and decision making
Reading and interpreting technical documents or regulations
Writing reports, proposals, or technical documentation
Leading a team or coordinating multiple priorities
Communicating effectively with clients, team members, and stakeholders
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities

Work Environment Requirements

Must be able to work outdoors in adverse weather conditions (heat, cold, rain, snow, etc.)
Must be able to travel up to 50% per year
May work in environments with loud noises, dust, or hazardous materials
Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
Office work environment
Potential for longer days up to 12 hours in duration.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

Work Schedule:
HGL office work is dictated by a 5-day work week; however, fieldwork schedules will deviate based on job requirements and may require longer hours and weekends.

Office Type:
In-office 5 days per week in either our Billings, MT or Helena, MT offices.

Travel:
50%

A favorable pre-hire drug test and physical are required.

All positions are subject to a pre-hire education and driving record verification.

MORE ABOUT HGL AND THE OPPORTUNITY

At HGL, we share a drive and vision to restore natural resources and provide ongoing stewardship of our environment to benefit present and future generations. We believe that we can make a difference in improving the world we live in through collaboration, teamwork, and a positive work environment. This unites and empowers us to strive for excellence in all our endeavors.

The exceptional quality of our people is key to our strength. We value our employees as individuals and as important members of our team. We offer a work environment that is flexible, inclusive, and dedicated to creating a sustainable future. By cultivating a culture of innovation, we’re able to adapt and augment our services to solve complex environmental and natural resources challenges.

Projects at HGL primarily span the United States and its territories, tackling problems associated with emerging contaminants (like PFAS), radiological contamination, and military munitions, along with chemical contamination in groundwater, surface water, sediments, and soil.

With over 550 employees, HGL is large enough to execute high-profile projects, but small enough to develop personal working environments with our talented team members. By joining HGL, you will be working toward restoring the environment and protecting our future.

HGL - WE INVEST IN YOU

It’s not just a job, it’s your career. HGL provides career growth opportunities via mentoring, training, education, and support for your certifications and licenses. Achieve your career goals and help HGL achieve its mission of restoring the environment to beneficial use for our clients and communities.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is seeking a Risk Assessor II to support environmental projects, including hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste; PFAS; mining; and military munitions response program projects nationwide. The Risk Assessor II will prepare human health risk assessments and/or ecological risk assessments in accordance with CERCLA, RCRA, and applicable state guidance, with support from HGL’s risk assessment team, including senior- and principal-level staff. Prepare tables, figures, and other data exhibits.
Author risk assessments, risk assessment work plans, and other technical deliverables.

Support remedial strategy design, including development of risk-based cleanup levels.

Description

Environmental Chemist

Put your analytical skills toward making a positive impact on the planet and your career! Join ICF in support of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) contract at the new Region 9 Laboratory in Corvallis, Oregon.

ICF is looking for an Environmental Laboratory Chemist in support of the USEPA Region 9 Environmental Services Assistance Team (ESAT) contract. ESAT provides analytical, quality assurance (QA), and technical support to USEPA programs such as Superfund and other programs requiring the identification, assessment, remediation, and regulation of environmental hazards. The team performs analysis on soil, water, air, waste, and tissue samples for chemical contaminants using USEPA-approved methods supporting EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment through programs such as the Drinking Water programs, Clean Water Act (CWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Superfund (CERCLA).

The Environmental Chemist
will apply their knowledge and work experience to primarily support the preparation and analysis of organic chemistry methods with possible cross-training on various inorganic analyses. All team activities must comply with EPA methods for various media (air, water, soil, biota) and environmental programs as well as the NELAC standard (2016). Job duties include sample preparation in support of and operation of GC-ECD, GC-FID, and GCMS to determine volatile and semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, Aroclors, and fuel hydrocarbon as well as new and emerging contaminants. The successful candidate must be able to work both independently and as member of a team.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related.
Minimum 2 years of laboratory experience using EPA-approved methodologies and instrumentation, preferably GC-FID, GC-ECD and GC/MS.
Excellent verbal, interpersonal and written communication skills, and the ability to think critically.
U.S. citizenship required per federal contract.

Solvent extraction experience using EPA methodologies and CLLE, SPE, ASE and other techniques.

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

Job Description

Position Summary:

The Associate Chemist prepares and analyzes environmental samples using standard analytical techniques according to approved scientific methodology in compliance with Eurofins Environment Testing Quality Assurance programs and standard operating procedures (SOPs). This position can be a physical job that may require standing for long periods, working with organic solvents, laboratory glassware and specialized equipment.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Performs routine lab tasks that provide experience and familiarization with methods, practices, and programs. These include:
Preparation of samples using standard techniques
Performing chemical analysis using standard techniques
Evaluation and quantification of data
Recording and reporting data and any unusual test occurrences to the supervisor
Performing routine instrument maintenance

Competency in complex instrumentation instrument specific software (training is provided)
Responsible for keeping personal training documentation (training records, IDOC/DOC) current and accurate
Responsible for timely completion of assigned/scheduled QC samples (MDL, LOD/LOQ, PT)
As required, documents NCMs for projects with quality issues
Understands and utilizes backlog reports to manage personal workload
Works under close supervision using routine and standard methods
Regular attendance and punctuality
Responsible for general housekeeping in work area
Proficient with IDOCs, for assigned methods carried out in the department
Responsible for performing job functions in compliance with Eurofins Environment health and safety and quality assurance standards
Demonstrates and promotes the company vision
Inventories and stocks laboratory supplies
Washes and inventories glassware
Purges analyzed samples
Assists in other areas of laboratory when needed
Additional duties as assigned

Follow and learn appropriate protocols in one or more of the following disciplines. This role will focus on PFAS Analysis and LC/MS.

Organic preparation
Metals preparation and analysis
PFAS sample preparation
HRMS sample preparation
Gas Chromatography
Liquid Chromatography
Mass Spectrometry
Radio Chemistry
Wet Chemistry
High Resolution preparation and analysis
Low Resolution preparation and analysis

This position is 2nd shift, Tues-Sat, 3pm -1130pm. Training will be M-F 7am-3:30pm.

Qualifications

Basic Minimum Qualifications

BS or BA in Chemistry or related field, Associate Degree, or 2 years of related laboratory experience in lieu of degree.
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.
Authorization to work in the United States without restriction or sponsorship

Ideal Candidates Will Have

Previous experience with PFAS and/or LC/MS
Previous experience in a lab or production setting
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
Able to interpret written materials and communicate findings effectively.
Demonstrated ability to identify issues, analyze root causes, and propose practical solutions.
Applies critical thinking to evaluate options and make decisions.
Effective collaboration skills to contribute to team goals and support department productivity goals
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines.
Effectively balances multiple tasks while maintaining accuracy.
Comfortable using mathematical formulas and tools to perform calculations and analyze data.
Consistently delivers high-quality work within established timelines and specifications.
Able to work independently, following written or verbal instructions with minimal oversight.
Strong interpersonal skills; able to coordinate tasks and communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.

Additional Information

Pay rate: $18-19/hour + 10% shift differential
